title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: document stage required at the moment of issue for originals to go into circulation
content:
## Scope

This rule of the Bills of Lading and Transport Documents product concerns the status a transport document must carry at the moment it is issued, for the originals of the set in force to be put into circulation by that issuance.

## Formal clause

1. Originals go into circulation at issue only when the document stands in the approval status at the moment of issue, that is, the status the document takes once the shipper's approval of the draft, or the deemed approval of an unanswered draft, has been recorded.
2. When the document is in any other status at that moment, no originals are put into circulation and the number is zero.

## Status-by-status reading

| Recorded status of the document at the moment of issue | Originals may go into circulation |
|---|---|
| Approval status | Yes |
| Draft | No; the number is zero |
| Issued | No; the number is zero |
| Surrendered | No; the number is zero |
| Released | No; the number is zero |
| Accomplished | No; the number is zero |
| Voided | No; the number is zero |

## Hypothetical cases

- A draft to which the shipper has not yet given its approval, and whose deemed approval period has not yet run out, is still in draft: an issuance at that moment would put no originals into circulation.
- A document whose draft reached deemed approval because the shipper did not answer stands in the approval status, in the same way as one to which the shipper gave its approval expressly.
- A document already issued earlier cannot put its originals into circulation a second time by a new issuance: its status is no longer the approval status.

## Points of judgement

- **Question:** The customer says the draft text was agreed by e-mail, but the document still shows draft. **Answer:** The recorded status governs; a document still in draft is not in the approval status.
- **Question:** Which moment counts? **Answer:** The moment of issue itself.
